clue.text: Noted character from the underworld

parts.note: a famous figure of Greek myth who was known for his music (hence 'noted') and who went down to Hades to bring back his wife

explanation.surface: A notorious gangland figure is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' reads as 'famous' and 'underworld' as organised crime, but the clue means a man of musical notes who visited the land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Thracian musician descended into Hades to try to rescue Eurydice, so he is a celebrated visitor to the realm of the dead.

clue.text: O to swim across the Channel! What an ass!

parts.note: across the Channel means in French, and the French verb for to swim is nager

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a fool trying to swim the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the Channel' is not a swim but France, so 'to swim' becomes the French nager.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of central Asia.

clue.text: Put Peter on the right animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting Peter on the rest places his piece above, that is first

parts.note: Peter Pan, J M Barrie's boy who never grew up

explanation.surface: An instruction to seat Peter on the correct beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or jaguar, especially a black one.

clue.text: What finally makes the score-draw

parts.note: the last goal in a match that brings the trailing side level

explanation.surface: A football pundit describes the decisive moment in a drawn game.
explanation.walkthrough: A score-draw is a drawn football match with goals scored (as on the football pools); the late goal levelling it gets a special name.
explanation.definitionFit: The goal that brings the scores level is the one that makes the match a draw.

clue.text: Only elastic can be replaced piece by piece

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in different places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that only the stretchy material can be swapped out one bit at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Done sectionally means done in separate parts, one segment after another.

clue.text: A number pursue subject of current interest

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the number pieces come after the subject in the answer

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A crowd chases a newsworthy subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical relates to matters in the news at present.

clue.text: Baby to which Brer Rabbit was much attached

definitions.text: Baby to which Brer Rabbit was much attached

parts.words: Baby to which Brer Rabbit was much attached
parts.note: in the Uncle Remus tales Brer Fox makes a sticky doll, and Brer Rabbit gets stuck fast to it

explanation.surface: Brer Rabbit is fond of an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much attached' sounds like affection, but Brer Rabbit was literally glued to the sticky doll made of pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticky black substance forms the first half of the name of the doll that trapped Brer Rabbit.

clue.text: Parking on a number plate

indicators.note: in a down clue the parking piece sits on top of the rest, so it comes first

parts.note: P is the usual sign for a car park
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A car is parked on a numbered registration plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number plate' suggests a car registration, but it splits: 'number' gives TEN and 'plate' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the small dish holding the bread at the Eucharist.

clue.text: Nessus was such a horseman

parts.note: Nessus of Greek myth was half man, half horse, a horseman in a literal sense

explanation.surface: A rider called Nessus is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Nessus was the creature killed by Heracles whose poisoned blood later killed the hero; 'horseman' means man and horse in one body.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessus was one of the mythical half-human, half-horse creatures.

clue.text: Bounty — great ship, note

parts.note: great means big or large
SS stands for steamship
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: The Bounty is described as a great ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounty' suggests the famous ship of the mutiny, but here it means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, much like bounty in its sense of liberality.

clue.text: He proclaims a sound reply to master's " What is a substantive ? "

indicators.note: a sound reply is one that sounds out: the spoken words are heard as the answer

parts.words: reply to master's " What is a substantive ? "
parts.note: a pupil answering a schoolmaster asking what a substantive is would say 'A noun, sir'

explanation.surface: A schoolboy gives a correct answer in a grammar lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'correct', but it signals that 'A noun, sir', the pupil's reply (a substantive is a noun), is spoken and heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is a person who makes public declarations, as on radio or at an event.

clue.text: A number or one who sings it

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A song is named, or else the singer who performs it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' that the singer sings is the voice part, the tenor line; the clue also hints that 'tenor' can name a number (a song).
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is the high male voice, and also the man who sings that part.

clue.text: If red, she's not ready

parts.note: a woman's name which, with 'red' added, becomes the name of the English king known as the Unready

explanation.surface: A woman who blushes is too flustered to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: Æthelred the Unready was a tenth-century English king; add RED to the girl's name and you have his name, so 'not ready' is his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding red to this girl's name gives Ethelred, the Anglo-Saxon king nicknamed the Unready.

clue.text: Imply or say to Adam how he fell ?

indicators.note: say means the words that follow are spoken, and the spoken words are heard as the answer

parts.note: speaking to Adam about his fall from Eden, you would tell him 'in sin you ate' (the forbidden fruit)

explanation.surface: A question of whether to hint, or tell Adam the story of the Fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly rather than state it.

clue.text: Magistrate finds it's upsetting to write a journal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the word read as its letters, with the apostrophe dropped
to pen something is to write it
a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: A magistrate is troubled by having to keep a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' looks like distress but turns ITS over, giving STI.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipendiary is a salaried professional justice, as opposed to an unpaid lay one.

clue.text: Salute welcomed by Venus de Milo

definitions.text: Salute welcomed by Venus de Milo

parts.words: Salute welcomed by Venus de Milo
parts.note: a military salute with rifles held upright; read literally, a gift of limbs would please the famously armless statue

explanation.surface: Soldiers greet a famous statue in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is a Greek statue missing both arms, so she would welcome anyone giving her arms.
explanation.definitionFit: This rifle drill is a formal military salute, and read as 'giving limbs' it suits the armless statue.

clue.text: Raised by the Tyne with the Psalmist's everlasting doors ?

definitions.text: Raised by the Tyne with the Psalmist's everlasting doors

parts.words: Raised by the Tyne with the Psalmist's everlasting doors
parts.note: Psalm 24 says 'Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors'

explanation.surface: A town on the Tyne is built with biblical doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like 'built', but it points to the psalm's 'lift up your heads, O ye gates'. The town is a Tyneside town facing Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateshead is a town on the south bank of the Tyne, and its name reads as the gates' head the psalm lifts.

clue.text: Sweet yet minimally sour

definitions.meaning: a boiled sweet with a sharp tang
a single drop of something tart is the least sourness possible

explanation.definitionFit: A tart boiled sweet is named for being a mere drop of the tart substance.

clue.text: But this mod, con, need cause no heartburn

definitions.text: But this mod, con, need cause no heartburn

parts.words: But this mod, con, need cause no heartburn
parts.note: a household comfort, a 'mod con', which warms the house; the clue jokes that warming the middle of you is heartburn but this kind does not cause it

explanation.surface: A modern convenience is promised to be harmless to the digestion.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mod con' is British shorthand for a modern convenience in a house; 'central' heating suggests warmth in the middle of the body, which this does not bring.
explanation.definitionFit: A system warming a whole building from one boiler is the classic modern home comfort.

clue.text: Feature light-hearted Flora -quite a handful !

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
gay in its old sense means merry or light-hearted

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl named Flora is quite a handful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a girl's name and 'quite a handful' like a lively child; together they mean flowers making a small bunch held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of flowers, enough to fill one hand.

clue.text: Rain ruined part of Japanese outfit in E Africa

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the first word are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the obi is the broad sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: Rain spoils a kimono sash while in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, a city located in East Africa.

clue.text: You have a pain ? So so, you say ?

definitions.meaning: a sharp pain in the side, as from running

explanation.walkthrough: 'So so' looks like 'middling', but each 'so' is to be heard as 'sew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden pain in the side, and also a single loop of thread made in sewing.

clue.text: Point to the city of Paris indeed-what happened to it?

annotationWithheld.why: Point to the city of Paris indeed-what happened to it? (9): S (point) + TROY (the city of Paris) inside DEED needs the single word 'indeed' to be both the container indicator 'in' and the fodder DEED, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Point to the city of Paris indeed-what happened to it?

clue.text: The Order of Dentists is a wash-out

definitions.meaning: the command a dentist gives a patient to swish water round the mouth
a quick wash with clean water

explanation.definitionFit: Dentists instruct patients to swill out the mouth, and that swilling is a quick wash.

clue.text: Bird writer

definitions.meaning: a fast-flying bird resembling a swallow

explanation.definitionFit: One name covers a fast-flying migrant bird and the Irish satirist Jonathan Swift.

clue.text: Terrible anger of the Wife of Cornwall

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of the next word are badly mangled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Duke's wife flies into a fearful rage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's King Lear, Lear's daughter Regan is married to the Duke of Cornwall; the surface makes her a temper-filled spouse, which she is.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear, Lear's cruel second daughter is the wife of the Duke of Cornwall.

clue.text: Distributes scrip issue ?

definitions.meaning: hands round portions among several people
a bonus issue of new stock certificates to existing holders

explanation.definitionFit: To hand out portions is the plain sense; a scrip issue literally gives out company stock to holders.

clue.text: And Ruth's boy leaves the Pepys musical to get drunk

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so those letters are taken out of the musical's title

parts.note: And So To Bed, a musical about the diarist Samuel Pepys, named after his diary's sign-off
in the Bible Obed is the son of Ruth and Boaz

explanation.surface: Ruth's son walks out of a show about Pepys to go drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AND and OBED from ANDSOTOBED leaves S, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a habitual drunkard, someone constantly under the influence.

clue.text: Bill just asks for it !

parts.note: an invoice merely requests the money, it does not take it

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is accused of inviting trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, and 'asks for it' like provoking trouble; read as an invoice, all a bill does is request the money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill or invoice is a request for settlement, the money handed over in return for goods.

clue.text: I did shy from translating this language

indicators.note: translating suggests turning words into something else, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone admits shrinking from translating a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is the Germanic tongue historically spoken by Ashkenazi Jews.
